headline: Real-time analytics pipeline hits v1.0.0 open-source and production-ready
summary: A new open-source real-time analytics pipeline built with Python has been released. It offers event tracking, real-time dashboards, and time-series aggregations.
details: The project, available on GitHub, provides a production-ready solution for SaaS products needing analytics. It allows for event tracking, real-time dashboards, and time-series aggregations, offering a customizable alternative to paid services like Segment or RudderStack.

The pipeline has achieved 150 out of 152 passing unit tests, with the two failing tests being pre-existing async timing issues. The developer emphasizes that no regressions were introduced in the v1.0.0 release.

The project encourages contributions and feedback, with users able to star the repository on GitHub to show support. Templates are also available for quickly answering FAQs or storing reusable snippets.
caption:
Can you build your own real-time analytics pipeline? A new open-source project just hit v1.0.0

The project, available on GitHub, provides a production-ready solution for SaaS products needing analytics. It allows for event tracking, real-time dashboards, and time-series aggregations, offering a customizable alternative to paid services like Segment or RudderStack.

The pipeline has achieved 150 out of 152 passing unit tests, with the two failing tests being pre-existing async timing issues. The developer emphasizes that no regressions were introduced in the v1.0.0 release.

The project encourages contributions and feedback, with users able to star the repository on GitHub to show support. Templates are also available for quickly answering FAQs or storing reusable snippets.

#Tech #OpenSource #Analytics #Python #SoftwareDevelopment

Source: DEV, Engadget, Wired
